sourceEvidence.text: Old English brægen named the brain, and related forms survive in other West Germanic languages. The modern intellectual-ability sense developed from the organ meaning. The remote origin is uncertain: Etymonline records competing accounts and disagreement about a suggested Greek skull-word connection. The lesson can explain the Old English organ meaning without presenting that contested comparison as a proven borrowing or ancestor.
